question: What will be Donald Trump's approval rating on Election Day 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the Silver Bulletin approve average itself, 24 days ahead, during the slow 2026 decline (40.4 in Jan, 38.29 in May, a term low of ~37.1 around Oct 3-5). As of Oct 8 the average had bounced to net -21.9 (approve ~37.6-37.9), mostly on one TIPP poll that will roll off. The slow downward drift (~0.3 pt/month) and the fading bounce put the median slightly below today's level, near 37.4. Partisans rallying before the midterm and mean reversion after a record low limit the downside. No matching human market: the Manifold and Polymarket candidates are about other events, and the Polymarket 'how low in 2026' and Kalshi RCP approval markets are near-miss contracts whose prices I couldn't retrieve. Web tools failed this run, so the evidence comes from repo traces dated Oct 6-8 and runs about 2 days stale.

calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the evidence (record low ~37.1 Oct 1-5, TIPP-driven bounce to ~37.5-37.9 by Oct 8, a ~0.3 pt/month downtrend). They differed only in how much drift to apply (medians 37.4-37.5) and in width (2.3-2.6). The exact Oct 8-10 level is a factual gap that cannot be settled without web access, so I carry it as about ±0.3 pt of extra uncertainty. On drift, I judge the fading of the one-poll bounce plus the year trend to slightly outweigh partisan-consolidation arguments, since there is no reliable pre-midterm approval rally in history. That gives a median of 37.4 with a slightly heavier low tail, also informed by Run 3's note that an earlier resolved forecast on this series ran high. The reference class matches all three runs. The dispersion is recomputed to include the level uncertainty. No matching human market was found by any run, and I could not check further. No escape mass: leaving the range would need a ~6 pt move in 24 days.
